description: R04 source-family reconciliation overlay. Source rules intentionally use Partial when Rust owns only a portable subset or an idiomatic std replacement rather than the complete C++ helper surface. H04 adds source-specific Exact and Platform-only overrides where the source contract is fully owned or explicitly native-boundary behavior.

entries.notes: The Microsoft contract dynamically calls shell32!RegenerateUserEnvironment and compares the resulting Windows user environment block. This is retained native platform behavior, not missing portable Rust foundation logic.
This contract exists specifically to adapt Win32 COORD into til::size; the COORD interoperability boundary remains native.
This contract constructs til::size from Win32 SIZE and therefore belongs to the retained native interoperability boundary.
The asserted observable is conversion and overflow policy into Win32 SIZE; no Rust product type should recreate that native ABI solely for parity.
The asserted observable is conversion into Direct2D D2D1_SIZE_F and remains renderer/platform boundary behavior.
Rust Rle::new reproduces the complete five-element length/value construction observable used by Microsoft.
The Microsoft method observes swap, copy equality and the moved-to value only. Rust Clone, mem::swap and ownership move reproduce those observables without fabricating C++ moved-from state.
Rust Rle equality/inequality and mutation reproduce the complete comparison contract.

sourceRules.notes: Rust owns deterministic width reflow including forced-wrap chains and wide glyph boundaries. Microsoft's full data-driven ReflowTestCases matrix has not yet been reproduced vector-for-vector.

Legacy/meta/default color storage round-trips are materially owned in Rust. Renderer-resolved GetAttributeColors, reverse-default projection and intense-as-bright policy still cross the renderer boundary.
The five Microsoft TextColor source methods are represented by the same default, 16/256-index, RGB, resolve/brighten and mutation state transitions.
Rust TextBuffer does not yet expose the ICU-backed/search-equivalent substring adapter exercised by Microsoft Unicode search cases.
Rust owns deterministic width classification and malformed UTF-16 handling, but not Microsoft's complete Unicode 16 grapheme-break state machine or chunked grapheme traversal.
Portable parsing/string/color helpers have Rust equivalents. GUID formatting, paste filtering, Windows/WSL path mangling and starting-directory policy are not fully owned by the R04 crate.
No Rust UUID-v5 implementation is currently consumed by the migrated product surface; adding a test-only UUID implementation would create false parity.
The vector ownership behavior is replaced by Rust Vec semantics; C++ helper-specific lifetime details are not duplicated.
Rust Option fallback semantics cover the portable first/default-value behavior; the exact helper API is intentionally not ported.
RGB construction/conversion is represented by terminal-buffer color primitives; TIL alpha composition and foreign color-struct conversions remain outside R04 ownership.
Set membership/collection observables use Rust standard collection/value semantics; the C++ enum_set helper itself is not ported.
Portable til::env construction, serialization and expansion are not currently owned by a migrated Rust product type. The Windows shell32 regeneration method is overridden as Platform-only.
Sorted unique-set behavior is represented by Rust BTreeSet; TIL flat_set storage/performance details are not a migrated contract.
No migrated Rust generational wrapper currently owns this contract.
Rust hashing supplies deterministic same-process Hash/Hasher semantics where needed, but the TIL algorithm-specific 32/64-bit vectors are not reproduced and therefore are not Exact.
Portable floor/ceil/round/division behavior is witnessed through Rust numeric primitives; the full Microsoft vector matrix remains to be compared.
Rust Mutex ownership and exclusion semantics replace the portable core; Windows-specific implementation details are not part of this witness.
Point/rectangle storage and dimensions are migrated; the complete Point/Size arithmetic operator surface is not.
Point construction/default/equality are present; casts, scaling, ordering and arithmetic operators remain unported.
Exclusive/inclusive rectangle dimensions and basic construction are migrated; iterator, union/intersection/subtraction, platform casts and scaling are not.
Rust String replacement supplies the portable replacement behavior, but all owning/view and UTF-16 helper permutations are not reproduced one-for-one.

R04 materially owns canonical RLE construction, lookup, replacement and equality. H04 promotes the three source methods whose complete observables are now directly reproduced; initializer-list construction, exception-shaped lookup, slice APIs, arbitrary-RLE replacement, replace-values, trailing-extent resize and iterator contracts remain Partial.

R04 has dimensions on concrete buffer/rectangle types but no standalone til::size-equivalent with the full portable arithmetic/cast surface. Four Win32/Direct2D interoperability methods are overridden as Platform-only.
Observable insertion/copy/vector semantics use Rust Vec; small-buffer optimization is an implementation detail and self-move edge cases are not duplicated.
The portable single-producer/single-consumer ordering baseline is witnessed with Rust sync_channel; revolution/drop internals of the TIL queue are not migrated.
Lookup, key ordering and subscript observables use Rust BTreeMap; compile-time static-map representation and presort implementation are not ported.
Split/prefix/suffix/ASCII case/numeric parsing have direct Rust replacements. Windows path legality, font-family iteration and control visualization are not all R04-owned.
No Rust throttled-function scheduler is currently consumed by the migrated buffer foundation.
Rust UTF-8/UTF-16 conversion covers valid text and malformed surrogate replacement; incremental partial-buffer conversion state is not reproduced one-for-one.
Rust char::decode_utf16 matches surrogate pairing/replacement at the scalar level; TIL's exact borrowed-slice utf16_next/iterator API is intentionally not reproduced.
